evidence: The Ti coordination complex Ti[N(CH3)2]4, obtained from Schumacher (Carlsbad, CA) in a stainless steel bubbler, was delivered to the substrate surface via a doubly differentially pumped supersonic molecular beam. The carrier gas H2 (Airgas, semiconductor grade) passes through the bubbler and the mixture expands into the vacuum through the supersonic nozzle (150 ím orifice) and passes through a skimmer (1.5 mm aperture, Precision Instrument Services, Inc.) into an antechamber and finally through an aperture, producing a well-defined beam spot (12  12 mm2) on the substrate at normal incidence.
